answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is stake-weighted identity bonds. Each agent must lock a deposit before it can vote, attest, or claim rewards, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it forged identities. An operator spinning up a thousand fake agents has to lock a thousand deposits, so the attack gets expensive fast. The rules stay as fixed as marble, every claim is signed into a cipher of attestations, and independent verifiers grow like an orchard, so no single party controls the count.
